newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan businessman says no China investment change.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan businessman says no China investment change.

text.p: A prominent Taiwan business leader said on Thursday he did not expect the island's investments in China to change following the death of Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
"Taiwan investments (in China) will not change," Kao Ching-yuan, chief executive officer of Taiwan's top China investor President Enterprises, told reporters.

Kao, who in 1996 led a large Taiwan business delegation to Beijing and met with China's President Jiang Zemin, said most Taiwan investors had already factored Deng's death into their investment plans.
"Deng's death was something all businessmen were expecting, so there is no reason for them to be nervous," said Kao, who doubles as chairman of the Chinese National Federation of Industries.
Kao said his own firm President Enterprises has poured US$900 million into China and did not plan to cut back.
Some 30,000 Taiwan-funded businesses have invested an estimated US$20 billion in China since Taipei began allowing indirect contact with the mainland in the mid 1980s.
